title: Chapter 104 — Inventory: What's Really in the Building
intro: Statuses decoded, counts and shrink, and selling with inventory truth.

sections.title: Inventory Statuses Decoded
sections.content:
On-hand is not the same as available. Sellable stock equals on-hand minus committed minus display minus damaged. Before you promise a customer delivery, check the sellable count — not just the system number.

Committed stock is already sold and waiting for delivery. Display units are floor models that may or may not be available for sale. Damaged units need inspection before they can be offered.

The rep who promises 'we have it in stock' based on the raw on-hand count and then discovers it is committed to another customer has just created a complaint.

sections.title: Selling With Inventory Truth
sections.content:
When stock is low, say so honestly. 'We have one left in stock. If you want it, I can reserve it right now.' Real scarcity is a legitimate closing tool.

When stock is out, offer alternatives. 'That model is on backorder for about 3 weeks. I can either hold that for you at today's price, or show you a comparable model that is in stock and ready for delivery this week. Which would you prefer?'

Never promise what you cannot deliver. Check the system. Verify the status. Then speak.

sections.title: Inventory Turns and Floor Health
sections.content:
Inventory turns measure how quickly product moves through the store. Higher is better — it means product is selling, not sitting. COGS divided by average inventory gives you the turn rate.

As a salesperson, you can influence turns by selling what is in stock rather than always special-ordering, by knowing which floor models have been sitting too long and recommending them to the right customers, and by flagging slow-moving inventory to your manager for promotional consideration.
